abstract.text: The vacuum expectation values of conserved currents play an essential role in the generalized hydrodynamics of integrable quantum field theories. We use analytic continuation to extend these results for the excited state expectation values in a finite volume. Our formulas are valid for diagonally scattering theories and incorporate all finite size corrections.

predecessors.why: The paper adopts its conservation-law, thermal-equilibrium, and pairing framework for currents and charges.
It uses TBA equations and dressing to express expectation values.
The paper shows the charge/current results follow from expanding the LM formula.
It extends this analytic-continuation idea to excited-state expectation values.

replications.why: Its asymptotic limit reproduces the charge-eigenvalue inverse-Gaudin-matrix formula from those works.

targets.cited_work: Asymptotic current formulas neglecting vacuum polarization
targets.why: It aims to include all finite-size corrections instead of only the leading asymptotics.

thesis.text: The exact finite-volume excited-state expectation values of conserved currents in diagonally scattering integrable quantum field theories can be obtained by analytically continuing the generalized-hydrodynamics/TBA formulas, replacing the ground-state pairing with a new pairing that adds discrete physical-particle residues and thus incorporates all finite-size corrections.

identity.title: Exact finite volume expectation values of conserved currents

question.text: How can one derive exact finite-volume excited-state expectation values of conserved charges and currents, including all finite-size corrections, by analytically continuing the generalized-hydrodynamics/TBA description? The hypothesis is that all ground-state formulas remain valid if the pairing is replaced by a new pairing containing discrete contributions from physical particles.
